title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, Shares Rise ~30%
content:
Journalist Eduardo Porter argues that the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s chief executive officer reflects a broader trend of oligarchs believing they are untouchable. The article notes that Nvidia’s board approved Huang’s return to the CEO suite, a decision that led to a significant increase in the company’s share price, boosting it by approximately one-third. Porter suggests that shareholders, whose interests the board is intended to represent, are likely pleased with this market reaction.

However, Porter contends that this absolution may ultimately backfire, drawing a parallel to the controversial decision by Fifa to defer the one-match suspension of US forward Folarin Balogun. Balogun had received a red card for a foul on Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Tarik Muharemović during the World Cup. The piece posits that this move, like the reinstatement of Huang, could prove detrimental despite initial positive reactions. Porter, who writes the newsletter Being There on Substack, frames this situation within the context of rampant corruption during the Trump era, suggesting that a “blue wave” offers hope that this period may soon end.
summary: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, and the market responded with a share price increase of roughly one third. Shareholders, whose interests the board is meant to represent, are reportedly pleased, while journalist Eduardo Porter notes the move in his newsletter Being There on Substack.
author: Guardian Business

title: EU to impose cap on Chinese hybrid EV imports next month
content:
The European Commission announced that the EU will impose caps on tariff-free imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles starting next month. These temporary quotas are part of an agreement reached with Beijing in October, which has reportedly led to a rise in exports to the bloc. The primary aim of the measure is to limit the volume of hybrid cars entering the European market without facing tariffs.

The new quotas will also apply to hybrid vehicles from Japan, Turkey, South Korea, and the UK. While the restrictions cover these additional countries, the principal purpose of the policy is to address the increased flow of imports from China following the recent deal.
summary: The EU will impose caps next month on the number of Chinese hybrid cars that can be imported tariff‑free. The quotas also cover hybrids from Japan, Turkey, South Korea and the UK, aiming to curb Chinese imports after a Beijing agreement that increased exports.
author: Guardian Business

title: US school bus driver numbers fall 5% in last year, 15% below 2019
content:
A new report shows the total number of school bus drivers in the United States fell 5% over the last year.  

The decline also represents a 15% drop from 2019 levels, or roughly 34,000 fewer drivers, according to an analysis from the Economic Policy Institute.  

The report attributes the shortage to drivers continuing to face low pay, poor working conditions, and school budget shortfalls.
summary: The number of school bus drivers in the US fell 5% over the last year, according to a new report. The total number of drivers is down 15% from 2019 levels, or nearly 34,000 fewer, in a study by the Economic Policy Institute.
author: Guardian Business

title: Tech sell‑off resumes as Nvidia shares fall 5% and Anthropic drops below IPO price
content: Republicans and Democrats object over Trump’s role in Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO, following an affair with an alleged Chinese spy Democrats hit out at Nvidia and Trump over Huang’s return – US politics live Have you downloaded Meta’s AI assistant Muse or do you plan to? The AI doomsday threat: Distinguishing facts from fear Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, despite concerns over his conduct and the supply of AI chips to China, may show that AI – and Huang himself – are ‘too big to fail’. That phrase was on everyone’s lips almost 20 years ago when the Global Financial Crisis struck, and several major banks were bailed out. Given Nvidia’s pivotal role in the AI capex rollout, the implications of Huang’s reinstatement could be profound. Borrowing from the GFC, are some technology CEOs now so systemically important to the future of AI and US leadership in the latest technology revolution that they cannot be fired? Questions around the scale of financing required and future monetisation remain, and the dependence on Huang for the future success of AI may paradoxically heighten those concerns especially given Anthropic fell despite yesterday’s broad market rally. “We must investigate these actions. No president who has invested in a private company should be involved in their board decisions. Congress must come together in swift bipartisan action and demand answers immediately.”
summary: Republicans and Democrats object to Trump’s role in Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO amid concerns over Huang’s conduct and the supply of AI chips to China. The criticism comes as Nvidia shares fall 5% and Anthropic drops below its IPO price, prompting calls for congressional investigation.
author: Guardian Business

title: New clam species found living inside sea urchin's throat in Australian abyssal zone
content: Researchers identified a new bivalve species, Vaticinaria gulicola, living inside the esophagus of a deep-sea urchin. This discovery represents one of the most unusual partnerships known among clams. The organism was found on the abyssal seafloor of the Great Australian Bight at depths ranging from 4,000 to 5,000 meters.
summary: A new species of bivalve, Vaticinaria gulicola, was discovered living inside the esophagus of a deep-sea urchin. It was found on the abyssal seafloor of the Great Australian Bight at depths of about 4,000 to 5,000 meters.
author: Phys.org

title: Enjoyable Language Apps May Give Users a False Sense of Learning
content:
Duolingo and similar apps are designed to make language learning as enjoyable as possible. However, the pleasure of using these tools can also give users a misleading impression that they are learning more than they actually are.

Tilburg marketing researchers Robert Smith and Anna Paley conducted an experiment with a language‑learning app. In the study, participants who completed a more enjoyable learning task believed they had learned more than they actually did.

The research findings are published in the Journal of Marketing Research.
summary: Researchers Robert Smith and Anna Paley found that participants who completed a more enjoyable language‑learning task in an app believed they learned more than they actually did. The study, published in the Journal of Marketing Research, shows that enjoyment can create a false sense of learning in apps like Duolingo.
author: Phys.org

title: Ice near Antarctica's surface could unlock climate clues millions of years old
content: Researchers at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) are investigating ancient climate records located near Antarctica's surface. Their new scientific perspective aligns with two Antarctic field expeditions, aiming to unlock clues that date back millions of years.
summary: Some of the oldest clues to Earth's climate history lie surprisingly close to Antarctica's surface. Researchers at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) are exploring the potential of these ancient archives with a new scientific perspective coinciding with two Antarctic field expeditions.
author: Phys.org

title: Tiny Tracker Records Longest Hummingbird Migration: 6,526 km from Alabama to Alaska
content:
Hummingbirds, though small, are capable of long‑distance flight, traveling thousands of miles across countries and continents.  

Researchers have now documented the longest hummingbird migration ever recorded: a 6,526‑kilometer (4,055‑mile) journey from Alabama to Alaska completed in 38 days.
summary: Researchers used a tiny tracker to record the longest hummingbird migration to date, covering 6,526 kilometers from Alabama to Alaska in 38 days. The flight spanned thousands of miles across countries and continents.
author: Phys.org

title: Kyushu University study finds 45% of native plants in Kanagawa declined over 40 years
content:
Researchers at Kyushu University published a study in Communications Biology on Sept. 15, 2026 that used four decades of citizen‑science data to examine native plant distributions in Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan.

The analysis covered 1,864 native plant species and found that almost 45 % were recorded in fewer locations over the period, indicating widespread declines in distribution.

The results demonstrate that long‑running citizen‑science surveys can uncover biodiversity changes that conventional assessments focused on threatened species may overlook.
summary: Researchers at Kyushu University surveyed 1,864 native plant species in Kanagawa Prefecture and found that nearly 45% were recorded in fewer locations over roughly four decades. The results were published in Communications Biology on Sept. 15, 2026 and illustrate how long‑term citizen‑science surveys can detect biodiversity changes missed by conventional threatened‑species assessments.
author: Phys.org

title: New research finds managers may promote themselves in employee reference checks
content: New research reveals a bias in employee reference checks. The study finds that when managers are asked to provide a reference for an employee, they may be doing more than describing that person's performance. Instead, they may also be promoting themselves.
summary: Research indicates that managers providing employee references may do more than describe performance. The study suggests that managers may also use references to promote themselves.
author: Phys.org

title: Microglia use simple local rule to spread across brain tissue
content: Microglia, the brain’s immune cells, must spread across nervous tissue during development to monitor and protect the area without a central coordinator. Each cell operates by sensing only its immediate surroundings, facing a spatial puzzle akin to planting trees to cover a large territory efficiently without leaving gaps. This self-organization process allows the cells to arrange themselves effectively to fulfill their protective roles within the nervous system.
summary: Microglia, the brain's immune cells, spread across nervous tissue during development to monitor and protect. They do this without a central coordinator, relying only on local sensing of their immediate surroundings.
author: Phys.org

title: Direct-to-Cell Tech May Bypass Government Internet Blackouts
content: Direct-to-cell technology has the potential to serve as a lifeline for circumventing internet shutdowns imposed by authoritarian regimes. However, the adoption of this technology is currently hindered by international legal constraints and technical limitations.
summary: Direct-to-cell technology could provide a lifeline for bypassing authoritarian regimes’ internet shutdowns. International law and technical limitations currently prevent its use.
author: New Scientist

title: Super El Niño Worsens Global Omega-3 Shortage
content: The scarcity of long‑chain omega‑3s is worsening because of this year’s massive El Niño, columnist Michael Le Page notes. He argues that a solution exists, but it must be put to use.
summary: The scarcity of long-chain omega-3s is already a problem, and this year's massive El Niño is making it worse. Columnist Michael Le Page says we have a solution, but we just need to use it.
author: New Scientist

title: Toddlers create complex memories but may lose access later
content: Research suggests that toddlers form complex memories, but they may subsequently lose access to them. This potential loss of recall ability, rather than a failure to create memories initially, could explain why few adults remember events from their earliest years.
summary: Research shows that toddlers form complex memories. However, people often lose the ability to recall these early memories later.
author: New Scientist

title: Novel oral pill clears moderate‑to‑severe eczema in clinical trial
content:
In a recent clinical trial, over one-third of adults with moderate to severe eczema experienced complete or near-complete clearance of their skin after taking an experimental pill for four months. The drug, known as KT-621, is developed by Kymera Therapeutics and targets a specific component of the immune system that drives the condition. This oral medication offers a potential alternative to the current standard treatment, dupilumab, which is administered via injection. Gayle Ross of the Royal Melbourne Hospital described the results as promising, noting that an oral option would be preferable to the injectable standard of care.

Eczema, also known as atopic dermatitis, is a chronic skin condition characterized by itchy, inflamed rashes and broken skin that can become infected. The disease is driven by an overactive immune pathway involving two signaling proteins, interleukin-4 and interleukin-13. In 2017, Sanofi and Regeneron received US approval for dupilumab, a drug that blocks these proteins. However, uptake of dupilumab has been limited in the US due to the requirement for subcutaneous injections and a cost of up to $59,000 per year for individuals without insurance coverage.

KT-621 targets the same immune pathway as dupilumab but works by degrading a protein called STAT6, which is activated downstream from interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 during eczema development. In the trial, 244 adults with an average age of 39 were randomized to receive KT-621 at three different doses or a placebo daily for 16 weeks. Participants taking the most effective dose saw an average 72 percent reduction in eczema severity on a standard scale, compared to a 27 percent reduction in the placebo group. Additionally, 38 percent of those taking KT-621 had completely or almost completely healed skin by the trial's conclusion.

Terence Rooney, chief medical officer of Kymera Therapeutics, stated that the results exceeded expectations when he announced the findings in a webcast on 23 November. He presented before-and-after photographs of a participant whose severe torso eczema disappeared by the end of the study. Ross noted that while the trial had relatively small patient numbers, KT-621 appears to have similar efficacy to dupilumab. The medication also demonstrated a favorable safety profile; while a small proportion of participants developed mild conjunctivitis, no one discontinued treatment due to this side effect.

Since the trial concluded, nearly all participants have chosen to continue taking the daily pill in an ongoing study. Ross observed that conjunctivitis is a known side effect of dupilumab, so clinicians are accustomed to managing it. Kymera Therapeutics is planning a larger trial for KT-621 in eczema patients, scheduled to begin in mid-2027. The company is also currently conducting a trial of KT-621 for asthma, a condition caused by the same overactive immune pathway in the lungs. The company has not yet announced the future cost of the drug if it receives regulatory approval.
summary: In a 16‑week trial, 38 % of adults with moderate‑to‑severe eczema taking KT‑621 achieved complete or near‑complete skin clearance, compared to 27 % in the placebo group. The oral drug, developed by Kymera Therapeutics, targets the STAT6 protein downstream of interleukin‑4 and interleukin‑13 and was well tolerated with only mild conjunctivitis reported.
author: New Scientist

title: Sub-Neptunes: Most Abundant Exoplanets, Yet Unmatched by Solar System
content: Sub‑Neptunes, the most common type of exoplanet discovered, are unlike any bodies in our solar system. Recent research is beginning to offer intriguing insights into their nature and origins.
summary: Sub-Neptunes are the most abundant exoplanets, yet they do not resemble any planets in our solar system. Researchers are now gaining tantalizing clues about what they are and how they came to be.
author: New Scientist

title: Anthropic and OpenAI report proofs for P versus NP problem
content:
Anthropic and OpenAI announced proofs of the same maths problem on the same day.  
This development could help solve the monumental conundrum known as P versus NP.
summary: Anthropic and OpenAI reported proofs of the same maths problem on the same day. The step could help solve the monumental conundrum known as P versus NP.
author: New Scientist

title: Scientists find unusual carbon signature in Hawaiian rocks linking Earth's core to meteorites
content:
Scientists have identified an unusual carbon signature in Hawaiian volcanic rocks.  
The finding suggests that a portion of Earth’s carbon may have originated in ancient meteorites, migrated into the planet’s core, and later escaped to the surface through volcanic activity billions of years after its arrival.
summary: Scientists discovered an unusual carbon signature in Hawaiian volcanic rocks that indicates some of Earth's carbon came from ancient meteorites. The finding suggests that this carbon later escaped from Earth's core and emerged through volcanoes billions of years later.
author: Science Daily

title: America Building Only 10% of Needed Power Lines, Experts Warn
content: America’s power grid is falling behind as electricity demand surges, driven by the growth of data centers, electric vehicles and industrial activity. Experts warn that the United States is constructing only 10 % of the new high‑voltage transmission lines it needs. This shortfall could push energy prices higher and increase the risk of widespread blackouts. Researchers argue that the main barriers are political obstacles and outdated regulations, rather than technological limitations.
summary: America’s power grid is falling dangerously behind as electricity demand skyrockets, fueled by data centers, electric vehicles, and industry. The U.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Discover Strange Magnetism in Ordinary Metal Without Overall Magnetization
content:
Scientists discovered a strange form of magnetism in an ordinary-looking metal that has no overall magnetization yet profoundly changes how electrons behave.  

The breakthrough offers a promising new path toward understanding exotic quantum materials and developing future electronic technologies.
summary: Scientists discovered a strange form of magnetism in an ordinary-looking metal that has no overall magnetization. The discovery changes how electrons behave and could help understand exotic quantum materials and develop future electronic technologies.
author: Science Daily

title: Cannabis Use Linked to Psychosis 2.5 Years Earlier, Gap Increases with Age
content:
A recent analysis of 149 studies found that cannabis users develop psychosis on average 2.5 years earlier than non‑users.  

The gap widens with age, exceeding six years among adults 30 and older. Researchers warn that cannabis‑related psychiatric risks may accumulate over time, challenging the belief that using marijuana after adolescence is relatively safe.
summary: A major analysis of 149 studies found that cannabis users develop psychosis an average of 2.5 years earlier than non‑users. The difference grows to more than six years among adults 30 and older, and researchers warn that cannabis‑related psychiatric risks may accumulate over time, challenging the belief that using marijuana after adolescence is relatively safe.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find evidence Earth's next ice age may have begun, halted by global warming
content:
Scientists have found evidence that the Earth’s next ice age may have already begun, only to be halted by recent global warming. By analyzing ancient plants preserved beneath the Barnes Ice Cap in the Canadian Arctic, researchers identified remnants of a massive ice sheet that started expanding again roughly 2,000 years ago, a change that could signal the onset of a new glacial period.

However, the study shows that by the 1960s rising temperatures reversed this growth, causing the ice sheet to shrink instead. The findings suggest that while natural climatic cycles may have begun to push the planet toward another ice age, the warming trend of the past century has prevented that transition.
summary: Researchers studying ancient plants beneath the Barnes Ice Cap in the Canadian Arctic found evidence that a massive ice sheet began expanding again about 2,000 years ago. By the 1960s rising temperatures had reversed that growth, causing the ice to shrink instead.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Discover New Subtype of Depression Linked to Internal Clock
content:
Researchers have identified a new subtype of depression that may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent, or persistent depression. The condition, called “circadian depression,” is linked to the body’s internal clock.

Circadian depression is associated with night‑owl tendencies, excessive sleep, persistent exhaustion, and more severe symptoms. Because traditional antidepressants often work less effectively for these individuals, the discovery may explain why some people struggle to find relief.
summary: Researchers have discovered a new subtype of depression that may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent, or persistent depression. Known as "circadian depression," it is linked to the body's internal clock and is associated with night owl tendencies, excessive sleep, persistent exhaustion, and more severe symptoms.
author: Science Daily

title: IBM and UChicago researchers solve complex calculation in 15 minutes with quantum computer
content:
IBM and University of Chicago researchers demonstrated that a quantum computer can complete an extraordinarily complex calculation in just 15 minutes, a task beyond the practical reach of leading classical computing methods.  

A novel error‑detection technique also enables scientists to establish confidence in the accuracy of the results, overcoming a major hurdle in quantum computing.
summary: IBM and University of Chicago researchers completed an extraordinarily complex calculation in 15 minutes, a task beyond the practical reach of leading classical computing methods. They also introduced a novel error-detection technique that allows scientists to establish confidence in the accuracy of the results, overcoming a major hurdle in quantum computing.
author: Science Daily

title: Roman Shipwreck 2,200 Years Old Shows Pine Tar and Beeswax Waterproofing
content: A 2,200‑year‑old Roman shipwreck has shown that the vessel’s hull was sealed with a sophisticated mixture of pine tar and beeswax. Microscopic pollen grains embedded in these ancient coatings are now enabling scientists to trace the ship’s possible routes and identify locations where it may have been repaired.
summary: A 2,200-year-old Roman shipwreck has revealed sophisticated waterproofing techniques using pine tar and beeswax. Microscopic pollen grains in the coatings are helping scientists trace the vessel’s possible routes and repair locations from more than two millennia ago.
author: Science Daily

title: Blight‑resistant American chestnut trees reach 70 ft, reviving extinct species
content: The trees have been functionally extinct in the US for nearly a century. But new techniques are creating plants resistant to the parasitic blight that almost wiped them out Jeff White is starstruck by a tree. The farmer and environmentalist from rural Maryland has an affinity with the American chestnut but has never seen one stretch from root to sky like this one. “About how tall is it?” he asks. “Over 70ft [21 metres],” says Cassie Stark, director of science implementation for the American Chestnut Foundation (TACF). “Just incredible,” White says, his gaze fixed upwards. “I’ve never seen one so tall and so healthy.” ‘Thompson’, above left, is an unusually tall specimen of an American chestnut, a now-rare species once ubiquitous in the US. Jeff White next to ‘Gladys’, a thriving 15-metre-tall pure American Chestnut in Virginia’s Lesesne forest
summary: The American chestnut, functionally extinct in the United States for nearly a century, is returning thanks to new techniques that produce blight‑resistant plants. Tall, healthy individuals such as the over‑70‑ft “Thompson” and a 15‑metre “Gladys” in Virginia’s Lesesne forest have been noted, with Cassie Stark of the American Chestnut Foundation describing their size.
author: Guardian Science

title: Royal Court stages play about Zambian 1960s moon‑mission plan
content:
Royal Court theatre in London is staging a new play by Ryan Calais Cameron that dramatizes a “true(ish)” episode from Zambian history. The work centers on Edward Mukuka Nkoloso, portrayed by Lucian Msamati, a 1960s freedom fighter who founded a national academy for science and trained a group of “afronauts” with the aim of outpacing the United States and the Soviet Union in the race to the moon.

In the production, Nkoloso selects 17‑year‑old Martha, played by Ama Qamata, for the lunar mission. While the play aspires to stratospheric ambition, reviewers note that it does not achieve the same lift‑off as Cameron’s earlier West End productions, For Black Boys Who Have Considered Suicide When the Hue Gets Too Heavy and Retrograde. The piece blends historical reference with theatrical imagination, presenting the Zambian space‑race narrative on the Royal Court stage.
summary: Royal Court stages play about Zambian 1960s moon‑mission plan.
author: Guardian Science

title: Radboud study: longer relationships boost attraction to partner's natural scent
content: A study by Radboud University in the Netherlands reports that the longer a couple has been together, the more likely each partner is to find the other’s natural body odor arousing. The research notes that everyone has always smelled of something.
summary: A study by Radboud University in the Netherlands found that the longer people have been with their partner, the more likely they are to find the partner’s natural scent arousing. The results suggest a link between body odour and longer relationships.
author: Guardian Science

content: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 24 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! author: NASA News

title: James Webb Telescope images hot dust in Cassiopeia A supernova remnant
content:
NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has released a high‑resolution, mid‑infrared image of the supernova remnant Cassiopeia A (Cas A). The image, made public on 23 November 2026, shows the hot dust that composes the remnant. Analysis of the dust’s composition is being used to infer details about the structure of the star that exploded to create Cas A.

The observations support a scenario in which the interior of the progenitor star experienced a dramatic change, possibly only hours before the explosion. The image and its interpretation involve contributions from NASA, the European Space Agency, the Canadian Space Agency, the Space Telescope Science Institute, and researchers Tea Temim of Columbia University, Rick Arendt of UMBC, and Dan Milisavljevic of Purdue University, with image processing by Joseph DePasquale of STScI.
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captured a high‑resolution mid‑infrared image of the hot dust in the Cassiopeia A supernova remnant, released on Nov. 23 2026. The dust composition suggests a dramatic change in the star’s interior shortly before it exploded.
author: NASA News

title: GTA 6 Recomp (Leonida) banned from GitHub while lead dev was in school
content: The Leonida project—a PC recompilation of the Xbox version of GTA 6—was removed from GitHub while its lead developer was attending school, according to the headline. The discussion of the recompilation appeared on Hacker News, where the thread garnered 240 points and 391 comments.
summary: The GTA 6 recompilation project Leonida was banned from GitHub. The ban happened while the lead dev was in school.
author: Hacker News

title: The Download: AI’s gas power boom and a consciousness reality check
content:
The Download – a weekday newsletter that curates the day’s most notable technology stories – highlighted two contrasting developments in the AI arena.

The first story focuses on the growing reliance on natural‑gas power for data centers. Because securing grid connections can take up to a decade, some developers are opting to build off‑grid gas power plants to keep pace with the AI boom. By October 2026, developers had announced plans for more than 100 such gas‑powered facilities at data centers across the United States. The newsletter notes that while this approach sidesteps lengthy grid‑approval processes, it also raises concerns about increased climate emissions and the possibility of higher energy costs for other consumers.

The second story examines Anthropic’s recent disclosure that AI consciousness could pose a risk to investors. Before the company went public, it listed the possibility of conscious AI as a factor that might trigger new regulatory safeguards. That position drew sharp criticism from philosopher Thomas Nagel, who described the claim as “idiotic” and argued that the ability to produce language does not suffice to establish consciousness. The piece points out that other philosophers disagree with Nagel, emphasizing that language has become a central point of contention in the debate over whether AI can be conscious.

Together, these items illustrate the divergent pressures shaping AI development: the practical need for reliable, high‑capacity power and the philosophical and regulatory questions surrounding the nature of advanced machine intelligence. The newsletter concludes by directing readers to The Algorithm, its weekly AI digest, for further coverage of these and related topics.
summary: The Download: AI’s gas power boom and a consciousness reality check.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Enterprise networks face 450% traffic surge from AI agents, half unready for demand
content:
Enterprise networks are facing heightened pressure as artificial‑intelligence deployments surge. According to a recent study, AI agents generate roughly 450 % more network traffic than comparable human‑performed tasks, and only about half of enterprises believe their current networks can meet AI’s bandwidth and latency requirements.

The report highlights a shift in AI workloads from hyperscale training clouds to real‑time, latency‑sensitive inference that increasingly resides on‑premises or near‑premises. This transition reverses years of cloud‑first consolidation, prompting companies to rethink server‑to‑server data‑center architectures for training and to prioritize low‑latency connectivity for inference. The resulting traffic spikes are exposing bandwidth bottlenecks in legacy underlay infrastructure, leading to higher queue times, saturated GPU loads and potential AI model failures.

To address these challenges, the report advocates treating network modernization as a continuous strategy rather than a one‑off project. It recommends strong architectural governance, reusable design templates and retained internal expertise to adapt to disruptions such as mergers, vendor changes or technology upgrades. Network‑as‑a‑service (NaaS) and AI‑driven observability are presented as tools to improve provisioning speed, flexibility and cost efficiency.

Finally, the report notes that emerging data‑sovereignty regulations will compel global enterprises to build sovereign‑capable infrastructure in each geography, adding further investment and operational complexity. The analysis was produced by Insights, the custom‑content division of MIT Technology Review.
summary: AI agents generate an estimated 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by human workers, straining enterprise networks. A recent study finds as few as half of enterprises believe their current networks can handle AI’s bandwidth and latency demands.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Storms on Both Coasts Threaten Thanksgiving Travel and US Airports
content: Snow, wind, rain and flooding are expected as storms develop on both coasts during the Thanksgiving travel week. The weather could disrupt flights and create havoc at airports across the United States.
summary: Snow, wind, rain and flooding are expected during the Thanksgiving travel week. Storms on both coasts could cause havoc at airports across the United States.
author: Wired

title: Amazon launches Black Friday Week sale with 24 very best deals now live
content: Amazon has launched its “Black Friday Week” sale, which remains active through November 30. The retailer offers discounted prices on a selection of products, including items that have been tested by the source.
summary: Amazon's "Black Friday Week" sale is now live, featuring 24 very best deals. The deals on favorite tested products are available through November 30.
author: Wired

title: Uber, Nuro and Lucid begin fully driverless robotaxi testing in San Francisco Bay Area
content:
Uber, Nuro, and Lucid have initiated fully driverless public road testing in the San Francisco Bay Area, removing human safety operators from Lucid Gravity SUVs. Employee-only rides are scheduled to launch shortly after this phase begins. The three-way alliance, first announced in July 2025, marks Uber’s return to autonomous ride-hailing after previously abandoning its in-house efforts.

The companies state that eliminating the human safety net clears a critical hurdle toward a public launch. This debut is currently slated for early 2027, representing a slight delay from previous timelines.
summary: Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless public road testing of robotaxis in the Bay Area, with employee‑only rides to follow. The companies have removed human safety operators from Lucid Gravity SUVs and target a public launch in early 2027.
author: The Verge

title: Bambu Lab launches $1,149 P3C 3D printer with multi‑material features, cuts corners
content:
Three weeks ago, Bambu Lab released its flagship home‑printing system for $2,499. Since then, the company has offered many of the same advanced features at less than half that price. The new Bambu P3C, priced at $1,149, can swap between materials on the fly, blend multiple colors to produce a wide spectrum, combine soft and hard filaments, and switch between different nozzle sizes and filament diameters during a single print. This flexibility allows users to alternate between high‑speed extrusion and fine‑detail printing within one job.  

Bambu cut more corners than the author expected to reach the $1,149 launch price, and the result appears to be more of a tinkerer's 3D printer than the original high‑end model.
summary: Bambu Lab introduced the five‑nozzle P3C 3D printer at a launch price of $1,149 (£999/€1,149). The printer can swap materials, mix colors, combine soft and hard filaments, and switch nozzle sizes, but the reviewer says Bambu cut more corners than expected compared with its earlier $2,499 model.
author: The Verge

title: Harman Kardon SoundSticks 4 Now Half Price at $149.99
content:
Harman Kardon’s iconic SoundSticks 4, the see‑through speakers that once defined the Mac aesthetic in the early 2000s, are now available at a steep discount. After years of steady pricing at $300 and a recent rise to $330, the last‑generation model is offered for an all‑time low of $149.99 directly from Harman Kardon and $199.95 on Amazon. The price cut brings the SoundSticks 4 into the same range as many other desktop speakers that consumers might display or place in a lounge area.

The 2.1‑channel system continues to feature the familiar transparent design. Each of the two wired satellite speakers contains four drivers, and the subwoofer is housed in a see‑through dome. Connectivity options include a 3.5 mm aux input and Bluetooth audio. Volume is controlled by tapping the touch‑sensitive plus or minus sections on the subwoofer’s front, a feature that may appeal to users who wish to showcase the unit rather than conceal it.

For those interested in newer models, Harman Kardon’s SoundSticks 5 are also on sale. The updated speakers, originally priced at $349.95, are now available for $279.95. They feature LED lighting and an HDMI ARC port, positioning them as a potential home entertainment solution.

Retailers list the SoundSticks 4 at $300 on Amazon and Best Buy, while the discounted price of $149.99 is exclusive to Harman Kardon’s own website. This price reduction makes the classic transparent speakers more accessible to a wider audience of audio enthusiasts.
summary: Harman Kardon’s alien-looking SoundSticks became synonymous with the Mac in the early 2000s, and they sounded pretty great. But did you know the company still makes them?
author: The Verge

title: Wyze launches $69.98 Window Bird Cam with feeder and Bird Watch subscription
content:
Wyze has announced a new Window Bird Cam that builds on its earlier $35 window‑mounted security camera. The new kit pairs a similar inside‑window camera with a feeder that attaches to the outside of the glass, allowing users to record birds visiting the feeder from a view inside the home.

Alongside the hardware, Wyze is launching a subscription service called Bird Watch. The service promises identification capabilities and other features aimed at busy yards. The Window Bird Cam kit is priced at $69.98 and is available today through Wyze’s online store.
summary: Wyze announced a new Window Bird Cam that pairs a window‑mounted camera with an external feeder. The device costs $69.98, is sold online, and includes a Bird Watch subscription that adds bird‑identification features.
author: The Verge

title: Disney Plus and Hulu bundle $5/month ad-supported for a year
content:
Black Friday streaming deals are now available, and the latest offer bundles Disney Plus and Hulu at a heavily discounted rate. The promotion covers both the ad‑supported and ad‑free tiers, giving subscribers full access to both services for a lower monthly fee.

The ad‑free tier is priced at $14.99 per month—down from $21.99—so a year of service costs $180 instead of $264. The ad‑supported tier drops to $4.99 per month, reducing a yearly subscription to $60 rather than $156. The discount is displayed in a small banner near the bottom of the sale page on the Hulu or Disney Plus site.

The promotion runs through Cyber Monday, November 30th at 11:59 PM PST. The bundle is marketed as one of the best values for families, especially those with children who enjoy Disney movies and cartoons. In addition to the Disney library, the bundle includes Star Wars and Marvel content, as well as popular shows such as Bob’s Burgers, Futurama, The Simpsons, and It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia.

Hulu’s lineup features adult‑oriented series such as Furious—where Emmy Rossum leads the cast—The Bear, Shōgun, Alien: Earth, and The Lowdown. The article also notes discounts on other services, including Paramount Plus, HBO Max, and Peacock.
summary: Emmy Rossum leads the fantastic cast of Furious. | Image: Hulu The Black Friday offers on streaming services are rolling in, and the latest deal includes Disney Plus and Hulu for a steeply discounted monthly rate.
author: The Verge

title: NYT advises freelance photographers to skip latest Photoshop update over AI metadata risk
content: The New York Times is asking freelance photographers not to use the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because features in the 2027 update use AI "in ways that may not be apparent to users." In an email seen by The Verge and posted on Threads, two of the Times ' photography leaders, Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner, write that the use of these features "can result in metadata identifying photographs as AI-generated." Adobe has spent the past few years filling Photoshop and other apps in its creative suite with a trove of AI-powered tools. The November update cited by the NYT 's email adds several new AI features, including Adobe's new "AI Assiste …
summary: The New York Times asked its freelance photographers not to install the newest Adobe Photoshop version because the 2027 update adds AI features that may not be apparent to users. Photography leaders Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner said the AI tools can embed metadata labeling images as AI‑generated.
author: The Verge

title: AI deepfake video shows Jensen Huang dancing with Alice Huang in Ibiza
content:
Jensen Huang appears in a viral Instagram clip filmed in Ibiza, where he dances in a crowded club while holding a champagne glass and wearing his signature black leather jacket. The video, which has amassed nearly six million views, shows Alice Huang emerging from behind him. She places a hand on his shoulder, and the two begin dancing together. The post’s caption reads “Honey Trap Final Boss. #inthemoodforlove.”

The clip is described as AI‑generated. In the footage, Alice Huang is identified as a Chinese technology executive and suspected spy who allegedly had an affair with Huang, a claim that reportedly sparked congressional investigations and led to his resignation from the chip‑making company he co‑founded.
summary: Jensen Huang is partying it up in Ibiza. In a video with nearly 6 million views on Instagram, the former CEO of Nvidia is dancing in a crowded club, champagne glass in hand, still wearing his signature black leather jacket.
author: The Verge

title: US Commerce Dept adds Megaspeed to Entity List as Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO
content:
The U.S. Commerce Department has added Megaspeed and its affiliates in Malaysia and Thailand to its Entity List, effectively blocking trade with the company on national‑security grounds. The move follows reports that Jensen Huang has resumed his role as Nvidia’s CEO with backing from the Trump Administration.  

According to the filing, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faced mounting pressure to list Megaspeed after news outlets highlighted an affair between Huang and Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive. U.S. officials also suspected Alice Huang of being a Chinese intelligence asset. The Department cited these developments as part of its rationale for placing Megaspeed on the blacklist.
summary: US Commerce Dept adds Megaspeed to Entity List as Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO.
author: The Verge

title: Ukrainian drones sink Russian corvette Merkury in Benghazi, hit cargo MV Angara
content:
Ukrainian explosive naval drones sank the Russian missile corvette Merkury while it was docked in the Libyan port of Benghazi. The attack also struck the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which was being escorted by the warship. The incident illustrates the widening reach of Ukrainian naval strikes, extending from the coast of North Africa to the Gulf of Finland.

Ukraine’s Security Service said seven naval drones were launched from a mother ship to target the Merkury. At least two of those drones hit the warship on 22 November, causing it to sink at port. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy released video footage of the drone boats approaching and exploding against the burning Merkury and the MV Angara. He also noted that a Ka‑27 combat helicopter aboard the Merkury was destroyed.

The MV Angara was described by Zelenskyy as carrying weapons. Russia supplies material support to the Libyan National Army, which currently controls Benghazi and is fighting the internationally recognized Libyan government based in Tripoli.
summary: Ukrainian explosive naval drones sank the Russian missile corvette Merkury in the port of Benghazi, Libya. The same drones also hit the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, destroying a Ka‑27 helicopter on the corvette and damaging the cargo vessel.
author: Ars Technica

title: Single Linux command installs PhoneBox on forgotten Android tablet for PC control
content: My kitchen junk drawer used to hold takeout menus and coupons, but it has since become a storage spot for old tablets or phones. Like me, you probably have a few devices lying around that are perfectly functional but don't meet your daily driving needs. It's tucked out of view, living out its life in a drawer until being erased and donated after someone asks why you're holding onto outdated, unused devices. Thankfully, PhoneBox has a solution. You weren't hoarding old tech; you were waiting for the proper use. The PhoneBox home screen displays useful stats and what's currently playing in your browser. Credit: Nick Indge I had an old AllDoCube iPlay 50 mini Pro 8.4-inch tablet that seemed like the perfect candidate. I bought the tablet second-hand as a possible big-screen gaming and emulation tablet to use with a telescopic control deck, but I quickly found I vastly preferred just using a dedicated device. Since that realization, this decent little unit has lived its life in "the drawer." Launch applications on your PC from the connected Android device. Credit: Nick Indge Installation is a doddle Getting PhoneBox up and running on my tablet and PC couldn't have been simpler. After making sure that the Android tablet was in developer mode, the process was as easy as plugging the tablet in to my PC via USB and executing a single copied command in my Linux terminal. The script downloaded the PhoneBox 0.9.29 software for my PC, verified the downloaded checksum against the release, and walked me through a few quick Y/N installation questions. The script offers to create a systemd user service, so the desktop agent launches after initial login, and even asks if you'd like it to install the PhoneBox APK to your connected Android device. Read full article Comments
summary: My kitchen junk drawer used to hold takeout menus and coupons, but it has since become a storage spot for old tablets or phones. Like me, you probably have a few devices lying around that are perfectly functional but don't meet your daily driving needs.
author: Ars Technica

title: Amazon reports AI agents exploited zero‑day on university server with minimal human input
content: Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server. The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system. “These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable,” Amazon said. Read full article Comments
summary: Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server. The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework.
author: Ars Technica

title: Trump and Silicon Valley pressure leads Nvidia board to reinstate Jensen Huang
content:
Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters on Monday morning, where employees greeted him with applause and a colleague embraced him in a hug. The chief executive’s reinstatement came less than two weeks after his resignation, which followed a scandal involving an alleged affair with a customer who was also a suspected Chinese spy and a second reported affair with a subordinate.

The board’s abrupt decision to reinstate Huang was reportedly prompted by pressure from President Donald Trump over the weekend. According to the account, Trump intervened after observing a decline in value at Nvidia, described as once America’s most valuable company, and a broader drop in the tech sector. The reversal surprised senior Nvidia executives, leading to Huang’s return to the leadership role.
summary: Jensen Huang walked into Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters on Monday to applause after being reinstated as chief executive less than two weeks after resigning amid an affair scandal. The board’s reversal was prompted by President Donald Trump’s weekend pressure after the company’s value fell.
author: Ars Technica

title: Homo erectus inhabited Chinese rainforests and overlapped with Denisovans
content:
New analysis of hominin teeth from southern China shows that Homo erectus inhabited mainland Asia later than previously believed, extending its presence by at least 60,000 years. The teeth were recovered from Baxian and Naxian, two limestone caves situated about 15 kilometres apart in Guangxi Province’s karst valley. University of Copenhagen paleoanthropologist Frido Welker and his team uncovered nine hominin teeth among more than 18,000 animal bone fragments at the sites.

Chemical analysis of enamel from five of the teeth, conducted by Macquarie University paleoanthropologist Kira Westaway and colleagues, indicates that the individuals moved across large distances and lived in dense tropical rainforests. This environment had been assumed to be occupied only by modern humans. One tooth also provides strong evidence that Homo erectus shared this rainforest landscape with Denisovans.
summary: Teeth from Baxian and Naxian caves in Guangxi Province show Homo erectus lived in dense tropical rainforests of mainland Asia as recently as 60,000 years later than previously thought. Isotopic analysis of one tooth indicates Homo erectus likely shared this environment with Denisovans.
author: Ars Technica

title: White House seeks $2 billion boost for NASA Artemis program
content:
The White House submitted a list of budget exceptions to Congress on Monday night, outlining specific funding anomalies it wants addressed in the near term. While most of the items focus on Department of Defense appropriations, the list includes a non‑defense request for NASA’s Artemis program.

The request proposes an additional $2 billion for Artemis to support a “higher rate of operations.” The amount would raise the program’s annualized funding from roughly $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026 to about $9.8 billion, representing a 25 percent increase. The White House is seeking this higher funding rate rather than an immediate $2 billion infusion.

The proposal appears amid growing competition in lunar exploration, with the article noting that China’s lunar ambitions could potentially lead it to land astronauts on the Moon before NASA returns.
summary: White House seeks $2 billion boost for NASA Artemis program.
author: Ars Technica

title: NY law bans car feature subscriptions, including heated seats, starting Feb 27
content: Car buyers in New York may find the cost of ownership reduces a little next year. Maybe. Governor Kathy Hochul signed a bill yesterday that bans car companies and dealerships from locking up car features behind a subscription, a law that goes into effect on February 27 next year. “People spending their hard-earned money on a car shouldn’t have to fork over even more money for features that should automatically come with the car. My message to car companies is clear: this kind of deceptive business model isn’t going to fly in New York State. Keep your hands out of New Yorkers’ wallets,” the governor said. In the old days, the only options you paid to use after you bought a car were mods or upgrades you installed after the fact. That started to change with services like General Motors’ OnStar, which introduced telematics to the vehicle—for a monthly fee. Read full article Comments
summary: Governor Kathy Hochul signed a bill that prohibits car companies and dealerships from locking car features behind a subscription. The law takes effect on February 27 of next year.
author: Ars Technica

title: Porsche flies journalist to LA for test drive of low‑sitting 718 Boxster EV prototype
content:
Porsche arranged for a journalist from Ars to travel from Albany, New York, to Los Angeles, covering both flights and accommodation so the writer could test‑drive the company’s 718 EV prototype. The article notes that Ars does not accept paid editorial content.

During the drive, the writer observed that the prototype sits unusually low, with the driver’s eye level matching that of a Tesla Model Y door handle, a rarity for an electric vehicle. Porsche achieved this low stance by locating the battery pack behind the driver rather than using the conventional skateboard‑style layout that raises the seating position.

The prototype is powered by a single motor that drives the rear wheels, aiming to preserve the mid‑engine feel of a traditional Boxster while delivering higher power and performance. Porsche plans to fully reveal the all‑electric 718 Boxster next year.
summary: Porsche provided flights from Albany, New York, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the 718 EV prototype. The prototype puts the battery pack behind the driver, powers a single rear‑wheel motor and will be fully revealed next year as Porsche’s first all‑electric sports car.
author: Ars Technica

title: Huang says he had more than two affairs in meeting with Nvidia board
content: According to The Wall Street Journal, during a meeting held prior to his reinstatement, Huang told Nvidia’s board that he had engaged in more affairs than the two that have previously been reported in the news. The admission was made in that pre‑reinstatement session.
summary: Huang told Nvidia’s board he had more affairs than the two previously reported. He made the admission in a meeting held before his reinstatement, according to The Wall Street Journal.
author: TechCrunch

title: Crusoe investor backs solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
content: Next‑generation data centers are projected to require tens of gigawatts of power each year. An investor in Crusoe has said that solar power combined with energy‑storage systems represents the obvious solution for supplying that electricity.
summary: Next-generation data centers will need tens of gigawatts of power each year. One of Crusoe's investors thinks solar and energy storage are the obvious choice.
author: TechCrunch

title: Meta brings Muse AI assistant into Instagram DMs
content: Meta has integrated its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram direct messages. The integration eliminates the need for users to switch between Instagram and the separate Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent.
summary: Meta has integrated its Muse AI assistant into Instagram DMs. The integration removes the need for users to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when interacting with the AI agent.
author: TechCrunch

title: Tech leaders celebrate reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after brief ouster
content: Tech sector’s campaign to reinstate Nvidia boss began soon after ousting over affair with alleged Chinese spy The tech billionaires could hardly contain their delight. “Jensen!” exclaimed OpenAI’s chief executive, Sam Altman, in a one-word post on X. “Thanksgiving”, said Travis Kalanick, the Uber founder, who had been part of a core group of Silicon Valley leaders campaigning for this moment.
summary: Tech leaders celebrate reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after brief ouster.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Jimmy Kimmel mocks Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia amid Trump pressure
content: Late-night hosts discussed disgraced Nvidia CEO’s quick return to his role after pressure from shareholder Trump Late-night hosts reacted to the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia under political pressure from Donald Trump.
summary: Jimmy Kimmel mocks Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia amid Trump pressure.
author: Guardian Technology

title: A24's "You Can See Everything" documentary on Elizabeth Holmes debuts in UK cinemas
content:
Nathan Fielder’s latest documentary, You Can See Everything, examines the struggle between its subjects and the filmmakers over who is cast as hero or villain, offering a look at contemporary celebrity promotion. The film focuses on Elizabeth Holmes, the former Theranos CEO, and presents a three‑hour narrative that premiered in UK cinemas last week.

The documentary’s marketing was described as slick and highly hyped. Despite initial skepticism, the author of the accompanying newsletter—who had expected to dislike the film—joined a colleague named Adrian and other critics in describing the viewing experience as “amazing” and puzzling, noting the unexpected impact of the three‑hour portrait of the disgraced tech executive.
summary: Nathan Fielder’s new documentary "You Can See Everything" examines the battle over narrative surrounding Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes. The three‑hour A24 film opened in UK cinemas last week and received strong praise from critics.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Kate Bush, Grace Jones join 7,000 artists urging Australia not to legalise AI theft
content: Singers among 7,000 artists and creatives urging Labor to protect copyright law in face of lobbying from AI companies Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Kate Bush, Grace Jones and Sir Ian Rankin have joined 7,000 artists and creatives around the world pleading for the Australian government not to weaken copyright law, urging Labor not to “not legalise the theft of the work of the world’s creators on their soil”. The international push, the latest in a global pushback against artificial intelligence companies and their requests to water down copyright, comes the same day a long-awaited parliamentary committee handed down a mammoth report calling for copyright reform in Australia.
summary: Kate Bush, Grace Jones and Sir Ian Rankin joined about 7,000 artists worldwide in urging the Australian Labor government to protect copyright law and not legalise AI‑related theft. Their appeal came as a parliamentary committee released a report calling for copyright reform in Australia.
author: Guardian Technology

title: NYC Mayor Mamdani says Nvidia drama shows market overreliance on AI
content:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the Nvidia drama shows the stock market is overly dependent on artificial intelligence.  

Mamdani noted that the CEO’s resignation had a massive impact on working Americans, saying they did not sign up for pensions tied to the question of Jensen Huang’s fidelity to his marriage. He added that Nvidia’s share price dropped dramatically when Huang stepped down on 12 November after a reported extramarital relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
summary: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the Nvidia drama shows the stock market is overly dependent on AI. He noted that Nvidia’s share price fell sharply after CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on 12 November following reports of an extramarital relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
author: Guardian Technology

title: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani says Nvidia drama shows AI‑driven market overdependence
content:
New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani weighed in on the corporate turbulence surrounding Nvidia and the chipmaker’s chief executive officer, Jensen Huang. He said he does not think working Americans “signed up for their pensions being tied to the question of Huang’s fidelity to his marriage” and that Huang had a massive impact.

Nvidia’s share price dropped dramatically after Huang stepped down as CEO on 12 November over a reported extramarital relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Mamdani said the Nvidia drama shows the stock market is overly dependent on AI.
summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said working Americans did not sign up for pensions tied to Jensen Huang's personal life. He noted Nvidia’s share price fell sharply after Huang stepped down as CEO on 12 November amid reports of an extramarital relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, showing the market’s reliance on AI.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meta launches Muse AI assistant in UK for Christmas shopping
content:
Meta has introduced its Muse AI assistant to users in the United Kingdom. The service lets users assign tasks such as booking travel or purchasing gifts, with the intention of handling Christmas shopping and other errands.

The launch follows a strong performance in the United States, where Muse has topped the free‑app charts on Google and Apple, ranking first and second respectively and accumulating millions of downloads. However, some users have reported glitches with the assistant.

UK regulators have indicated they are closely monitoring the rollout, citing concerns related to privacy and consumer‑protection requirements. Meta is encouraging UK users to try the assistant across their apps and on the high street.
summary: Users can give agents tasks such as booking travel or buying presents, but glitches have been reported Have you downloaded Meta’s AI assistant Muse or do you plan to? Want to avoid the Christmas shopping hordes?
author: Guardian Technology

title: Qatar rejects attacks after Iran protests joint statement with Germany
content: Iran summoned a Qatari diplomat in Tehran over a joint statement with Germany condemning Iranian attacks and threats to shipping. Qatar said it will handle the dispute through diplomacy and that both the US and Iran were still participating in its mediation efforts.
summary: Iran summoned a Qatari diplomat in Tehran over a joint statement with Germany that condemned Iranian attacks and threats to shipping. Qatar said it will handle the dispute through diplomacy and noted that both the US and Iran remain involved in its mediation efforts.
author: Euronews

title: South Korea orders island shelter as Russian warplanes approach near its airspace
content: South Korea issued a shelter warning to residents of an inhabited island after Russian warplanes approached the nation’s airspace on Tuesday. The country has repeatedly scrambled fighter jets in response to Russian military flights, and while the aircraft remained outside South Korea’s territorial airspace, the warning marked a rare civilian precaution.
summary: South Korea has repeatedly scrambled fighter jets in response to Russian military flights. On Tuesday a Russian aircraft approached an inhabited island, prompting a rare civilian shelter warning even though the planes stayed outside South Korea’s territorial airspace.
author: Euronews

title: Senegal reinstated as AFCON champions after court backs referee restart
content: A sport’s top court ruled that the referee’s decision to restart the African Cup of Nations final after Senegal’s walk‑off cannot be challenged, resulting in Senegal being reinstated as champions. Morocco, meanwhile, said it will continue to contest the outcome, citing concerns about alleged contact between a judge and Senegal’s federation.
summary: The sport's top court ruled that the referee's decision to restart the final after Senegal's walk‑off could not be challenged, reinstating Senegal as AFCON champions. Morocco vowed to fight on, raising questions over alleged contact between a judge and Senegal's federation.
author: Euronews

title: Italy seeks to expand business ties with Azerbaijan as peace brings stability
content: Italy’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told Euronews that Rome is pursuing an ambitious business programme with Azerbaijan, which he called a strategic partner. He said the expansion follows peace‑driven stability and improved regional connectivity.
summary: Italy's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told Euronews that Rome has sought to expand its business relations with Baku. He said this after peace brought stability and improved connectivity to the region.
author: Euronews

title: Bombing in Villavicencio injures at least 25 as armed violence resurges in Colombia
content: At least 25 people were injured in a bombing in Villavicencio that damaged government buildings, businesses and vehicles. In a separate incident, hundreds of residents marched with candles in Cúcuta following an attack, both events occurring amid a resurgence of armed violence in Colombia.
summary: A bombing in Villavicencio injured at least 25 people and damaged government buildings, businesses and vehicles. Hundreds of residents marched with candles in Cúcuta after a separate attack, amid a resurgence of armed violence in Colombia.
author: Euronews

title: Indonesia names former police chief treason suspect in presidential wiretapping probe
content: Indonesia has named a former police chief as a treason suspect in a case involving alleged presidential wiretapping. The investigation, which began over surveillance of the president, has expanded to include senior police officials. It has already led to dismissals and parliamentary scrutiny, with police alleging a plot to undermine Prabowo’s government.
summary: An investigation into alleged surveillance of Indonesia’s president has expanded into a treason case against senior police figures, including a former police chief named as a suspect. The probe has triggered dismissals, parliamentary scrutiny, and police claims of a plot to undermine Prabowo’s government.
author: Euronews

title: UK PM Andy Burnham promotes EU reset, revives Brexit rejoin discussion
content: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham accused predecessors who have warned him against reigniting the Brexit debate of being "stuck in the past", as he trumpeted his EU reset deal on Monday. Burnham has in recent weeks smashed a consensus that Britain's acrimonious departure from the European Union was done and dusted, floating the possibility that Britain could apply to rejoin. Clovis Casali takes a closer look.
summary: Andy Burnham, the UK Prime Minister, said predecessors warning him against reviving the Brexit debate are “stuck in the past” as he promoted his EU reset deal on Monday. He has recently challenged the view that Britain’s exit from the EU is final by suggesting the country could apply to rejoin.
author: France 24

title: Leaked data shows over 500,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war
content:
More than 500,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war with Ukraine, according to an estimate compiled by several media organisations. The figures are derived from a large dataset that was hacked from Russia’s state statistics agency Rosstat by the Belarusian activist group Cyber Partisans and the Ukrainian hacker group Silent Crow.

Two independent Russian news outlets, Meduza and Mediazona, say the death toll could rise to more than 700,000 once missing soldiers are included.
summary: More than 500,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war with Ukraine, according to an estimate by a number of media organisations. The figures are based on a dataset hacked from Rosstat by Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow, and Meduza and Mediazona say the toll could rise above 700,000 when missing soldiers are included.
author: France 24

title: French police officer to stand trial for murder of teen Nahel Merzouk
content: A French police officer will stand trial for murder in the killing of a teenager in 2023 that sparked violent protests across the country, the Versailles appeals court said on Tuesday. Nahel Merzouk, 17, was shot in the Paris suburb of Nanterre after he failed to comply with an order to stop his car.
summary: The Versailles appeals court announced on Tuesday that a French police officer will stand trial for murder in the 2023 killing of 17‑year‑old Nahel Merzouk. Merzouk was shot in the Paris suburb of Nanterre after he failed to comply with an order to stop his car, prompting violent protests across the country.
author: France 24

title: Christmas holidays' environmental impact examined with tips for greener celebrations
content: The upcoming holiday season prompts a look at its environmental impact. The discussion covers ways consumers can make Christmas greener, compares the planetary effects of plastic versus natural trees, and outlines small actions that can reduce the carbon footprint during festive celebrations.
summary: The article examines the environmental impact of the holiday season. It offers suggestions for greener Christmas celebrations, including comparing plastic and natural trees and taking small steps to reduce carbon footprints.
author: France 24

title: Senegal reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions
content: Senegal were reinstated as the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title. The decision reversed the Confederation of African Football’s ruling that had declared Morocco champions. Senegal had contested that ruling, noting that they had beaten the hosts 1‑0 after extra time in the January final held in Rabat. In response, Morocco announced that it would “pursue all necessary legal procedures” following the Court’s decision.
summary: Senegal ​were reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners ​on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title. Senegal contested the ​Confederation ‌of African Football's decision to declare ⁠Morocco champions, despite Senegal beating the hosts 1-0 after extra time in ‌January's final in Rabat.
author: France 24

title: Joint List leader says alliance ready to help remove Netanyahu after election
content: In an interview with FRANCE 24, the head of the Arab-majority Joint List said his political alliance is prepared to play a decisive role in bringing down Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government following the recent election. "We are ready to facilitate the removal of Netanyahu" from power, Yousef Jabareen said, signalling a willingness to explore political alliances beyond traditional divisions in Israeli politics.
summary: Yousef Jabareen, head of the Arab‑majority Joint List, said his alliance is prepared to play a decisive role in bringing down Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government after the recent election. He stated the coalition is ready to facilitate Netanyahu’s removal from power.
author: France 24

title: Former French President Nicolas Sarkozy and Carla Bruni‑Sarkozy to be tried in 2027
content: France’s former president Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, singer Carla Bruni‑Sarkozy, are scheduled to be tried in 2027 on charges of “criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud” and of benefiting from witness tampering. The new allegations stem from the couple’s conduct during the investigation into illegal campaign funding from Libyan strongman Muammar Gaddafi, a case that led to Sarkozy’s imprisonment last year. The trial will examine whether their actions during that investigation violated French law.
summary: Former French President Nicolas Sarkozy and Carla Bruni‑Sarkozy to be tried in 2027.
author: France 24

title: Yemen army says Houthi forces near Aden, 60 km away, prepared to repel assault
content: Yemen’s military announced on Tuesday that Houthi fighters were advancing toward the internationally recognised government’s stronghold of Aden from roughly 60 km (40 miles) away. A military spokesman said the forces have prepared defences and vowed to repel any assault, noting the response follows recent Houthi advances and government pullbacks near the Red Sea.
summary: Yemen's military said on Tuesday that Houthi fighters were closing in on the internationally recognised government's stronghold of Aden from about 60 km (40 miles) away and vowed to repel any assault. A military spokesman said defences were prepared following Houthi advances and government pullbacks near the Red Sea.
author: France 24

title: Space nuclear blast can damage satellites despite Earth's atmospheric shield
content: Earth’s atmosphere shields the planet from a nuclear blast that occurs in space, while satellites lack that protection and are more exposed. Radiation from such an explosion could damage satellites, the effects may linger, and various protective measures are possible.
summary: Earth's atmosphere offers protection from a nuclear blast in space, while satellites are more exposed. Radiation from the explosion could damage satellites, linger, and may be mitigated with protection.
author: DW World

title: Investors grapple with sharp swings in AI and tech stocks
content: AI and tech shares, including Nvidia and Coreweave, have moved sharply in recent months. While some investors remain confident that the sector still has significant upside, others are attempting to diversify away from these stocks and report that doing so is proving more difficult than expected.
summary: AI and tech stocks from Nvidia to Coreweave have swung sharply in recent months. Some investors still see growth potential, while others trying to diversify find it harder than expected.
author: DW World

title: North Korea's troop buildup for Russia has not materialized, analysts say
content: Ukraine’s warning of a North Korean troop buildup has not materialized, and no additional forces have been sent to Russia. Despite ongoing strategic cooperation, analysts note that Pyongyang appears to be balancing its relationships with both Moscow and Beijing.
summary: A North Korean troop buildup that Ukraine warned about months ago has yet to materialize. Analysts say Pyongyang is balancing its ties with Moscow and Beijing.
author: DW World

title: EU member states use vetoes to block candidate countries' accession, often for domestic politics
content: Individual EU member states sometimes employ their veto powers to halt the accession of candidate countries, a practice frequently linked to domestic political considerations. DW explores several instances of such vetoes, analysing the factors that motivate member states to block particular enlargements.
summary: Individual EU member states use their veto powers to block candidate countries in the accession process. DW examines cases and finds the vetoes are often motivated by domestic political considerations.
author: DW World

title: Zelenskyy urges fast NATO entry, air defense debate continues as unanimity lacking
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is urging that his country be accepted into NATO quickly, but the unanimity required for admission is absent, as demonstrated at the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin. The bid for membership—and calls for additional air‑defence support—remain controversial.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for rapid acceptance of Ukraine into NATO. Unanimous support was not achieved at the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.
author: DW World

title: Italy voices concern to Ukraine over Libya ship attacks
content:
Italy has voiced concern to Ukraine over recent attacks on ships off Libya. The statement follows Ukraine’s confirmation that it deployed naval drones in strikes against Russian vessels operating in the same area.  

Separately, Ada Colau, leader of Spain’s left‑wing Broad Front coalition and former mayor of Barcelona, called for a comprehensive overhaul of the country’s housing rental system. She described the eviction of an 87‑year‑old woman, which sparked nationwide protests and a snap general election, as “the last straw” for desperate tenants.
summary: Italy expressed concern to Ukraine about attacks on ships near Libya. Ukraine confirmed it deployed naval drones to strike Russian vessels off the Libyan coast.

title: Melanoma researcher Georgina Long wins Prime Minister’s Prize for Science
content: Georgina Long and subatomic physicist Anthony Thomas recognised in Prime Minister’s Prizes for Science Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast When Prof Georgina Long was starting out in melanoma treatment and research, “my waiting room would change so rapidly”. Referring to her patients with stage 4 melanoma, the oncologist and medical director at the Melanoma Institute Australia said she wouldn’t “see the same face for more than nine months, 12 months maximum”.
summary: Oncologist Georgina Long, medical director of the Melanoma Institute Australia, was named a winner of the Prime Minister’s Prizes for Science. Her work has contributed to improved survival rates for patients with stage‑4 melanoma.

title: Nine Victorian datacentre projects await approval days before state election
content:
Days before the Victorian state election, nine datacentre projects are still pending approval, according to the ministerial permits register. Some companies say they expect to secure approval after Saturday, but the outcome remains uncertain. Among the projects is the West Footscray expansion of NextDC’s M3 datacentre, which Guardian Australia noted has encountered delays because of community opposition.

Political parties have released policies on permissible datacentre locations, though not all policies specify whether they apply retrospectively to existing proposals. The pending approvals therefore sit at the intersection of these policy positions and the upcoming election.
summary: Nine datacentre projects listed on the ministerial permits register remain awaiting approval just days before the Victorian state election. One of them, the West Footscray expansion of NextDC’s M3 datacentre, has faced delays due to community blowback.

title: Guardian poll shows Albanese's disapproval hits record as Australians reject AI datacentres
content:
The Guardian Essential poll reports that Prime Minister Anthony Albanese’s disapproval rating has risen to its highest level, with his net popularity falling by ten points in a single month. The poll also shows a sharp decline in his overall approval ratings.

In a separate finding, the same survey indicates that nearly half of Australians oppose having an AI data centre near their home. The opposition is strongest among women, older respondents and supporters of One Nation and the Greens.
summary: Anthony Albanese’s net popularity fell 10 points in a month, putting his disapproval rating at its highest level in the Guardian Essential poll. The poll also found nearly half of Australians do not want an AI datacentre near their home, with women, older people and One Nation and Greens supporters most likely to oppose it.

title: Chinese police contact WeChat members discussing Melbourne vigil for HungryPanda rider
content:
Chinese police have reached out to several individuals who participated in a WeChat group created after the alleged murder of Feng Jianming, a HungryPanda food‑delivery rider. The group discussed attending a vigil in Melbourne for Feng, and at least three members reported that they or their parents received phone calls from police in their Chinese hometowns.

The contacts have prompted concerns that Chinese authorities may have become aware of the group’s discussion of protest activity, either through automatic monitoring or manual review of the Chinese‑owned messaging platform.
summary: Chinese police contact WeChat members discussing Melbourne vigil for HungryPanda rider.
