title: Malaysia to deport thousands of migrants to Myanmar after ICJ genocide ruling
content: Malaysia announced it will repatriate thousands of migrants and refugees to Myanmar. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the move will proceed even though the government recognizes that many of the asylum seekers have been victims of “atrocities” carried out by the junta in Naypyidaw. The decision was made days after the International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar had committed genocide against its Rohingya minority. Malaysia’s announcement follows the UN court’s finding of genocide against the Rohingya population.
summary: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia will deport thousands of migrants and refugees to Myanmar, acknowledging many asylum seekers were victims of junta atrocities. The announcement came days after the ICJ ruled that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya minority.

title: Trump ignored intelligence on alleged Chinese spy tied to Nvidia co‑founder
content:
The source states that Donald Trump’s reaction to sensitive information that contradicts his worldview is presented as mirroring his conduct toward a potential war with Iran. It further claims that his unwillingness to heed warnings of suspected Chinese penetration of the tech company Nvidia follows a pattern of the U.S. president ignoring sensitive intelligence that conflicts with his perspective.  

According to the source, Trump disregarded repeated information that Nvidia co‑founder Jensen Huang was having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, a situation described as threatening Washington’s goal of surpassing China in the global artificial‑intelligence race.
summary: Trump has repeatedly ignored intelligence that contradicts his worldview, including warnings of suspected Chinese penetration of Nvidia. He also disregarded repeated information that Nvidia co‑founder Jensen Huang was having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which threatened Washington’s goal of outpacing China in the artificial intelligence race.

title: Leaked data shows over 300 Russian troops killed while supporting Mali's junta
content:
Leaked records released exclusively show that 349 Russian personnel died in Mali over a three‑year period, a figure that exceeds three hundred. The documents also provide information about Russia’s military operations in other African countries.

One of the incidents detailed in the data is the assault on the northern town of Kidal on 25 April. According to a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps, who spoke anonymously, the attack began before dawn and caught the Russian fighters off guard. Within the first hour, insurgents overran checkpoints on the city’s outskirts and advanced toward the police station, where intense fighting broke out.

The witness described explosions and shouting throughout the engagement, noting that “nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.” The leaked data therefore links a high Russian casualty count to Moscow’s support for Mali’s junta and illustrates the volatility of Russian‑backed forces in the region.
summary: Leaked records list 349 Russian deaths in Mali over a three‑year period. The data describes a Russian‑backed attack on Kidal on 25 April, when insurgents overran outskirts checkpoints and fighting broke out at the police station.

title: NASA launches Discovery on classified STS‑33 mission for U.S. Military
content:
On November 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on a secret U. S. Military mission, designated STS‑33. The launch occurred at night, making it the third nighttime launch in the shuttle program and the thirty‑second mission overall. Five astronauts aboard the orbiter were tasked with deploying a classified payload for the U. S. Department of Defense.

The payload believed to have been released by Discovery is thought to be a type of spy satellite known as Magnum. The specific mission of the satellite in orbit remains classified, and the details of its operations are not publicly disclosed.

The shuttle program was conceived as a compromise between civilian and military objectives. NASA intended the vehicle to support scientific research, enable on‑orbit servicing of commercial satellites, and assemble components for a space station. The Department of Defense viewed the shuttle as a platform for deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites and other classified projects. Following the loss of the Challenger, it was decided that the shuttle would be used for military missions only when they were essential to national security, while other needs would be met with expendable launch vehicles.

During the STS‑33 mission, the crew also celebrated Thanksgiving in space. The holiday began with a malfunction of the shuttle’s toilet, which the astronauts spent most of the day repairing before enjoying a turkey together.

For additional space‑history content, readers can explore the full “On This Day In Space” archive and view related videos on YouTube.
summary: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.
